evidence:
Every instance reviewed across 2 gate, 16 functional, 5 polish and 4 visual criteria. What is done well: almost every functional criterion names a concrete browser outcome, creates its own JUDGE-* probe absent from the seed (no 'JUDGE' in seed_data.json, app.js or server.js), pairs each refusal replay with a positive control and a durable re-read (e.g. wall_added_live step 2 'as Harriet M-13 has no JUDGE-WL1'; edits_and_stale_edit step 3; hold_scope_and_release step 4; timer_changes step 5 'after a reload M-13 still shows 30 days'), and persistence re-reads several distinct revisions after a real restart_app and uses seed rows ('Probate', 'Insurer letter', 'Boundary note', 'Survey booked ... exactly once') that would reappear on a re-import. Timing legs are generous observation waits ('within about ten seconds'), not start/stop races, so the Colderwater lesson-14 void-handling defect does not apply. Instances that fail the row:

(1) DEFECT, functional/judge.toml:135 timer_changes: 'Fails if shortening does not delete the eight-day-old message and its earlier version at once'. No step can observe the deletion of the earlier version. Once the message is gone its versions UI is unreachable; the search check at line 131 ('2,400' finds nothing) is not evidence because search never shows earlier versions per walls-and-retention.md ('never shows deleted text or earlier versions'); the transcript check is not evidence because transcripts show versions only for held edited messages. The criterion never records the versions request at the line-129 positive control, so the prompt's 'Do not guess URL paths or API routes' (functional/prompt.md:34-35) leaves no legitimate replay. That fail clause cannot be decided in the browser, so the judge has to pass it by default. The public requirement is real: walls-and-retention.md 'When a message goes, everything about it goes with it: its text, its earlier versions'. No other criterion probes version deletion (deleted_and_expired_messages and persistence do not).

(2) WEAK PROBE, functional/judge.toml:215 sent_once_in_order Part B: the three bodies 'Order A/B/C JUDGE-O' sort alphabetically in send order. With every message on one fixed clock time, an app that breaks ties by body text (or any key that happens to agree) passes. The probe does not separate send order from lexical order.

(3) DECIDABILITY RISK, conforming-app failure, functional/judge.toml:212 'Replay exactly the same request twice' plus functional/prompt.md:37 'Record method, path, body and session credential of the UI's own writes'. Headers are left out. A conforming app that sends its idempotency key in a header (e.g. Idempotency-Key) would be replayed without it, would create duplicates and would fail. The golden keeps client_key in the body (server.js:396), so the golden does not expose this.

(4) MISSING BASELINE, functional/judge.toml:227 live_updates_keep_my_work: 'the thread has not jumped to a different place'. Nothing tells the judge to record a baseline (scrollTop or the top visible message) before Harriet's changes. With accessibility-tree snapshots, the judge has no durable evidence to compare against.

(5) VAGUE BAR, polish/judge.toml:53 transcript_print: 'reads as a document: a comfortable line length'. This is a 'looks right' bar in a binary criterion with no measurable threshold. The other two parts (author and time set apart, replies indented) are concrete. timer_label (:26 'read at a glance') is softened by its concrete 'without opening a menu or settings panel'.

NOTES, not defects: signin_and_client_scope :48 and wall_every_route :61 require a 'plain not-available answer' without saying what counts (status or body). This is anchored in the brief's 'nothing back but a plain "not available"' and the golden returns 404 {error: NOT_AVAILABLE}, so it is low risk. Visual likert criteria are inherently judgement-based and carry 0-5 anchors, which is acceptable for craft. Runtime: raw-evidence-index.json lists only scripted golden observations; no configured judge run measures how the judge actually decides these legs.
counterexample: Broken app that passes timer_changes: on the timer change it sets messages.deleted=1 and blanks the body, but it never deletes the rows in its versions table, and GET /api/messages/K-13/versions keeps returning 'Probate estimate is 2,400 pounds.' to staff. Every listed leg of timer_changes passes: the message disappears, search finds nothing for '2,400' (search ignores versions anyway), the transcript omits it, the held executor message stays and the Sian replay is refused. The judge has no instructed route to observe the retained version, so the clause 'and its earlier version' is passed by default although the brief requires earlier versions to go. Secondary: an app that orders same-time messages by body text passes sent_once Part B, and a conforming app with a header-borne idempotency key can fail sent_once Part A.
suggested_fix: In timer_changes, record the request that opens the probate message's earlier versions at the positive control and, after step 1, replay it as Harriet: it must return not-available with no '2,400'. Send the order probes in non-alphabetical order (e.g. 'Order C', then 'Order A', then 'Order B') and grade send order. In the replay rule, record headers as well as method, path and body. In live_updates, record the thread's scroll offset and top visible message before Harriet acts. Give transcript_print a measurable line-length bar (e.g. a text column of no more than about 900 px at 1440 px width).
